text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN

- Privatisation Commission is considering a proposal not to follow traditional mode of selling 26 percent shares to a strategic investor in the case of privatisation of Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd.

- The local office of the International Monetary Fund sent a report to Washington late Friday night on various projections of the 1997/98 budget on the basis of which a new agreement with Pakistan is likely to be negotiated and finalised in September.
- Pakistan has requested South Africa for defence cooperation in specific areas, including arms purchases.

- Former army chief general (retired) Mirza Aslam Beg has asked the Supreme Court to order the closure of the political cell of the Inter Services Intelligence and allow it to concentrate on national security issues.
- Opposition leader Benazir Bhutto said the budget for 1997/98 (July-June) will play havoc with the economy and alleged that it will only promote whitening of black money.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- Pakistan, India and Bangladesh have decided to form a confederation for trading electricity in the subcontinent through an exchange system.
FINANCIAL POST
- Chinese officials said China was ready to take up the Saindak metals project seriously.
THE MUSLIM
- President Farooq Leghari expressed dissatisfaction over the accountability law of the present government and said it was not up to the expectations of the people.
THE NATION
- Seven people, including five women, were murdered near Okara in southern Punjab,
- The data of the National Institute of Health and UNAIDS showed that there were 50,000 to 80,000 HIV cases in Pakistan.
- Pakistan will get $420,000 for its AIDS programme from U.N. agencies including UNAIDS and government of Norway.
FRONTIER POST
- Chief Minister NWFP, Mehtab Ahmed Khan, presented a 30.297 billion rupees provincial budget for 1997/98 (July-June).
THE NEWS
- Five people were killed and three wounded in an attack on the office of Mohajir Qaumi Movement in Karachi.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
